summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all seven paragraphs of the selected Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the narrative sequence, recognition exchange, repeated writing instructions, purpose and ability clauses, complete conditional chains, negations, promised and opposite outcomes, and the Shepherd’s repentance title. The simplified edition’s shorter syntax does not materially remove source content. Contextual repentance follows current policy without equating it with grief or adding doctrinal conditions. The notes retain the selected working readings while accurately distinguishing the supplied reports of correction layers, versional alternatives, editorial proposals, and Clement’s bounded quotation. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of the supplied evidence; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
